- Averages we see in pilot samples: avg prompt tokens ~220, avg completion tokens ~980.

- Budget: target range $30k–$60k / month initially. For benchmarking, our finance lead mentioned a target of roughly $10 / 1M tokens as a reference point but expects higher for long-context workloads.

Open questions for you: how do you recommend pricing for the 32k/128k requests (multipliers or separate SKUs)? Would dedicated/reserved capacity materially lower the $/1M at our starting volume? Also interested in any performance SLAs for 32k/128k contexts.

Alice — this is perfect, thanks for the detail. A few quick notes and a high-level cost/price framework while we prepare a formal quote: 

1) Hosted vs Dedicated (ballpark $/1M):
   - Hosted (pay-as-you-go / API): expect blended ~$14–$18 per 1M tokens at 150M scale for standard gen models; long-context handling (32k/128k) typically carries a 2–8x multiplier depending on model and batching.
   - Dedicated / Reserved capacity: with a commit (monthly/annual) we can get to ~$4–$8 per 1M tokens at this volume — biggest savings come from sustained concurrency and model affinity.

2) Long-context pricing guidance (rules of thumb):
   - 8k context: ~1.6–2.5x cost of baseline 1k/2k requests (due to larger KV cache and memory pressure).
   - 32k context: ~2.5–4x baseline.
   - 128k context: ~6–10x baseline and often requires special routing / dedicated memory-optimized hosts.

Given your avg prompt/completion (220 / 980) and 150M tokens/month, some quick math:
   - If blended price = $15 / 1M tokens (hosted), monthly spend ~ $2,250 (this is illustrative — blended means across short and long contexts).
   - If you wanted to peg to a target $/1M = $10, we’d likely need a committed dedicated plan + some model/quantization work (or reduce percent of 32k/128k calls).

Next steps I’ll take:
- Prepare a dedicated vs hosted cost model showing unit economics at 150M and 300M tokens.
- Show explicit multipliers for 8k/32k/128k and run a blended example based on the percentages you provided.
- Include options for fallbacks (route 128k to smaller specialized model or async job) to control costs.

I attached the pricing template (filled with the numbers you sent) and will loop in Solutions to validate the 128k capacity plan. Any additional detail (peak concurrency, percent realtime vs async) will help tighten the estimate.

I’ll aim to get the formal quote to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: acme_pricing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
